<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914805_theRebbe_603" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914805_theRebbe_603__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the second interpretation of "Lech Lecha" as an ascent from the lowest level, paralleling the journey of Yaakov after Tishrei, beginning from the heel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the second "Go for yourself etc. to the land" is</t>
    <t s="2">(according to the simple meaning of the verse30)</t>
    <t s="3">that this going is from below to above,</t>
    <t s="4">the going from your land, from your birthplace, and from your father's house, which is</t>
    <t s="5">(according to the simple meaning of the verse)</t>
    <t s="6">the land etc. of Terach</t>
    <t s="7">[the opposite of the concept of purity31],</t>
    <t s="8">the lowest level,</t>
    <t s="9">and from there he will go and ascend from below to above until the land that I will show you, which refers</t>
    <t s="10">(as above in section 1)</t>
    <t s="11">to the aspect of Malchus,</t>
    <t s="12">and until the aspect of "And he built there an altar to Havayah who appeared to him"32</t>
    <t s="13">(which is above the aspect of Malchus),</t>
    <t s="14">and until "And he built there an altar to Havayah" simply33,</t>
    <t s="15">the aspect of the supernal Havayah,</t>
    <t s="16">the concealed Havayah,</t>
    <t s="17">which is above the Havayah</t>
    <t s="18">(of below)</t>
    <t s="19">that appeared34.</t>
    <t s="20">And likewise, this is also the case in the service of "And Yaakov went on his way" within each person after the month of Tishrei,</t>
    <t s="21">that this going is</t>
    <t s="22">(not only in a manner of from above to below,</t>
    <t s="23">that he goes on his way from the festivals of the month of Tishrei to his way in matters of the mundane and weekday activities throughout the entire year,</t>
    <t s="24">but rather)</t>
    <t s="25">also in a manner of from below to above,</t>
    <t s="26">beginning from the power of his action,</t>
    <t s="27">and in the power of action itself, as it is in his heel,</t>
    <t s="28">the lowest level in the human body</t>
    <t s="29">[and it is even a matter of the opposite of life35,</t>
    <t s="30">similar to what was brought above regarding Terach, who is the opposite of purity],</t>
    <t s="31">and from there his journey begins from below to above,</t>
    <t s="32">which also affects his heel that it should hear Elokus</t>
    <t s="33">[and as it is written regarding Avraham, "Because (eikev) Avraham listened to My voice"36,</t>
    <t s="34">that even his heel (eikev) heard37.</t>
    <t s="35">And because this was the case with Avraham Avinu,</t>
    <t s="36">the power for this was given to every Jew</t>
    <t s="37">(similar to the concealed love within every Jew, which is an inheritance for us from our forefathers38,</t>
    <t s="38">and specifically from Avraham Avinu39)],</t>
    <t s="39">and from this is drawn</t>
    <t s="40">(in a manner of a journey from below to above)</t>
    <t s="41">the hearing</t>
    <t s="42">(the hearing)</t>
    <t s="43">of Elokus in all the faculties,</t>
    <t s="44">until the intellectual faculty in the head,</t>
    <t s="45">so that there will be in them a hearing that is above measure and limitation of intellect.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the service of dancing on Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah, beginning with the heels, empowers the entire year's ascent from below to above.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And also this matter of "And Yaakov went on his way"</t>
    <t s="1">(a journey from below to above)</t>
    <t s="2">begins after the month of Tishrei.</t>
    <t s="3">For the service of Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah</t>
    <t s="4">(the conclusion of the festivals of the month of Tishrei)</t>
    <t s="5">is with</t>
    <t s="6">(joy and)</t>
    <t s="7">dancing,</t>
    <t s="8">that the concept of dancing is</t>
    <t s="9">(primarily and begins)</t>
    <t s="10">in the legs,</t>
    <t s="11">and in them specifically in the heel of them.</t>
    <t s="12">And by the heels being lifted up</t>
    <t s="13">(they lift themselves)</t>
    <t s="14">and dance,</t>
    <t s="15">they also lift up the head</t>
    <t s="16">(and the intellectual faculty within it)40,</t>
    <t s="17">so that it too dances with great joy above measure and limitation.</t>
    <t s="18">And from this is drawn the power for the service of "And Yaakov went on his way"</t>
    <t s="19">(a journey from below to above)</t>
    <t s="20">throughout the entire year,</t>
    <t s="21">beginning from the power of action as it is in the heel</t>
    <t s="22">[including the matters that a person tramples with his heels41,</t>
    <t s="23">meaning matters for which</t>
    <t s="24">(for whatever reason)</t>
    <t s="25">he has no vitality in them</t>
    <t s="26">(similar to the simple meaning of the heel, which is a matter of the opposite of life)],</t>
    <t s="27">and from this he draws</t>
    <t s="28">(in a manner of a journey from below to above)</t>
    <t s="29">also to the intellectual faculty in the head,</t>
    <t s="30">as above.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section correlates the two interpretations of "Lech Lecha" with the two interpretations of "On the other side of the river your forefathers dwelt."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And the two aforementioned explanations of "Go for yourself from your land etc." correspond to the two explanations of "On the other side of the river your forefathers dwelt"42.</t>
    <t s="2">The explanation</t>
    <t s="3">[in the inner dimension of Torah43]</t>
    <t s="4">that "the other side of the river" is the aspect that is above</t>
    <t s="5">(also)</t>
    <t s="6">the aspect of "And a river went out of Eden"44</t>
    <t s="7">(Binah of Atzilus)</t>
    <t s="8">and the explanation of "On the other side of the river your forefathers dwelt etc." is that the root of the forefathers is from the other side of the river, above Atzilus, and from there they were drawn downward</t>
    <t s="9">(on the other side of the river,</t>
    <t s="10">meaning)</t>
    <t s="11">into the Z'eir Anpin of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="12">and until "And I led him throughout all the land of Canaan"45</t>
    <t s="13">the descent and drawing down into the aspect of Malchus</t>
    <t s="14">(as above in section 1, that the land of Israel refers to Malchus)</t>
    <t s="15">— the going from your land etc.,</t>
    <t s="16">which refers to the other side of the river,</t>
    <t s="17">to the land that I will show you,</t>
    <t s="18">is a journey from above to below46.</t>
    <t s="19">And the explanation</t>
    <t s="20">(as it is in the simple meaning)</t>
    <t s="21">that "the other side of the river" is the place of Terach,</t>
    <t s="22">and what is said "On the other side of the river your forefathers dwelt etc." is for disparagement</t>
    <t s="23">[as is proven from the words of our sages, of blessed memory47,</t>
    <t s="24">"He begins with disgrace etc. Initially our forefathers were idol worshippers etc., as it is said, 'On the other side of the river your forefathers dwelt etc.'"]</t>
    <t s="25">— the going from your land etc.</t>
    <t s="26">(the other side of the river)</t>
    <t s="27">to the land that I will show you,</t>
    <t s="28">is a journey and ascent from below to above48</t>
    <t s="29">(as above in section 3).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
